qualitative.filing_summary_10k: For fiscal 2025 (ended February 1, 2026), Home Depot reported net sales of $164.7 billion (up 3.2%) and net earnings of $14.2 billion, with growth driven largely by the SRS and GMS acquisitions contributing about $6.3 billion of incremental sales. Comparable sales rose a modest 0.3% amid continued macroeconomic pressure on home improvement demand, while gross margin and ROIC both declined slightly year over year. The company completed the GMS acquisition for about $5.5 billion, paid $9.2 billion in dividends, invested $3.7 billion in capital expenditures, and noted it experienced increased costs from tariffs during the year, which it says it partially mitigated through supply-chain diversification and pricing actions.
qualitative.filing_summary_10q: This is Home Depot's Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended August 2, 2026 (Q2 fiscal 2026). The excerpt provided is largely structured/XBRL cover-page and index data rather than narrative discussion, but it indicates the filing covers segment reporting, goodwill/intangible assets, debt and derivatives, stockholders' equity, and acquisitions, including references to the completed GMS acquisition and a smaller acquisition of Mingledorff's, Inc. in May 2026. The provided text does not include the actual MD&A narrative discussing quarterly results, so specific sales or earnings figures for the quarter are not available in these excerpts.
qualitative.filing_summary_8k: This 8-K, dated August 20, 2026, discloses executive leadership changes under Item 5.02: three named executives (William D. Bastek, Jordan Broggi, and Richard V. McPhail) had their responsibilities expanded to cover areas including private brands/merchandising, loyalty/credit/payments, and cross-business Pro coordination (Home Depot Pro, HD Supply, SRS, Construction Resources), as previously announced July 30, 2026. In connection with these expanded roles, the Board's compensation committee granted each executive a restricted stock award with a grant-date fair value of $500,000, vesting on the second anniversary of the grant date subject to continued employment.
qualitative.moat_explanation: The 10-K explicitly states Home Depot's brand is 'one of the most recognized brands in North America' with trademarks it believes have 'significant value,' and lists brand, product authority, and proprietary/exclusive brand relationships as 'distinct competitive advantages.' The filing also describes scale, supply chain network, and Pro relationships as advantages, suggesting a cost-advantage/scale component alongside the brand, but the excerpts emphasize brand and proprietary product differentiation most explicitly as durable differentiators; no single patent is described as essential, and the industry is repeatedly characterized as 'highly competitive, highly fragmented, and evolving,' tempering the strength of any moat claim.
red_flags: Comparable sales were roughly flat (0.3%) with comparable customer transactions down 1.0%, and management attributes softness to macroeconomic uncertainty and high interest rates pressuring home improvement demand
Company acknowledges experiencing 'increased costs as a result of tariffs' in fiscal 2025 and cannot predict future trade-policy impacts with certainty
ROIC declined from 31.3% to 25.7% and inventory turnover declined from 4.7x to 4.4x, partly due to higher debt from the SRS/GMS acquisitions

Share repurchases remain paused with no plans to resume in fiscal 2026 as the company works to reduce debt following large acquisition-related borrowing (aggregate senior notes outstanding of $48.8 billion)

Risk factors note an 'aging store base that requires maintenance, investment, and space reallocation' and warn that a growing shift to online/direct fulfillment could reduce in-store cross-selling traffic and pressure margins
Gross margin declined slightly (33.3% vs 33.4%) due to the inclusion of lower-margin SRS/GMS distribution businesses
